independent_deductions: At a fixed basepoint a, dy=fprime(a)dx is an exact linear function of the displacement dx. The finite change is Δy=f(a+dx)-f(a)=dy+o(|dx|). Treating dy as the exact finite change is generally false. The finite-difference quotient requires nonzero displacement; differential notation does not turn the approximate finite-increment relation into equality.

For cube root at a=64, f(a)=4 and fprime(a)=1/48, so at h=1 the tangent estimate is 4+1/48=193/48, approximately 4.02. At h=0.1 it is 4+1/480. The rescaling method is 4(1+h/64)^(1/3), with small variable h/64. Source methods 1 and 3 incorrectly use exact equality between cube root of 65 and the linear estimate. The exact rational cube discrepancy is (193/48)^3-65=577/110592>0.

For x>=64, fdoubleprime(x)=-2/(9x^(5/3))<0, so the tangent overestimates. Its magnitude is at most 1/4608 on that interval; Taylor gives absolute error at most h²/9216 for h>=0. This verifies the size and sign of the approximation without falsely treating it as exact. The cube-root derivative is evaluated at a positive basepoint; the finite derivative formula does not apply at x=0.

The listed six primitives differentiate correctly: -cos x for sin x; x^(n+1)/(n+1) for x^n when n≠-1 on an appropriate real-power interval; ln|x| for 1/x on each nonzero component; tan x for sec²x between poles; arcsin x for 1/sqrt(1-x²) on (-1,1); arctan x for 1/(1+x²) on all real x. Arbitrary real powers may uniformly be treated on x>0, though special integer/rational powers allow larger intervals. On x<0, derivative of ln(-x) is (-1)/(-x)=1/x. The proof labelled property 2 actually establishes property 3.

If Fprime=Gprime=f on a common interval, (G-F)prime=0 and MVT implies a single additive constant. A disconnected domain permits independent constants on its components: ln|x| plus a step of 1 only for x>0 has the same derivative as ln|x| on R without zero. Source wording constant factor is wrong for the additive difference. An indefinite integral represents an antiderivative family unless a representative/initial value is selected.

All substitution examples checked directly: derivative of (x^4+2)^6/24 is x³(x^4+2)^5; derivative of sqrt(1+x²) is x/sqrt(1+x²); derivative of exp(6x)/6 is exp(6x); derivative of -exp(-x²)/2 is x exp(-x²). These four identities hold for all real x. Global invertibility of u=x^4+2 is unnecessary to this indefinite primitive identity because the chain rule itself verifies it, including at x=0. The first source calculation adds +C only after an equality to a representative without +C; the family/representative convention should be consistent.

The derivatives of sin²x/2 and -cos²x/2 both equal sin x cos x, while their difference is exactly 1/2 by sin²x+cos²x=1. The antiderivative families agree after shifting their constants; using equal numerical constants does not make the two selected functions identical.

For 1/(x ln x), the real domain is (0,1) union (1,infinity). The substitution u=ln x gives primitive ln|u|, hence ln|ln x|+C on each interval with potentially separate constants. Source ln(ln x) is only real for x>1 despite stating merely x>0. At x=1/2 the integrand is the finite value -2/ln 2 but the supplied primitive is not real. x=1 must be excluded as a singularity. This is a source formula/domain error, not simply a missing derivation.
No external current claim or numerical lookup is needed; exact differentiation, rational arithmetic, and direct source-page comparison supply the witnesses.
